---
title: "Transfer Learning"
description: "Reusing knowledge learned on one task or dataset to improve learning on a related target task."
term: "Transfer Learning"
letter: "T"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Transfer learning starts with a model or representation learned elsewhere
and adapts it to a new but related task. This can reduce the labeled data
and compute needed compared with training from scratch.

## Technical explanation

Transfer learning reuses parameters, features, or learned structure from a
source domain or task. Common strategies include using a frozen pretrained
encoder as a feature extractor and fine-tuning some or all of its
parameters on target data. Benefit depends on source-target similarity and
the adaptation procedure.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Pretrained models can provide a strong starting point for specialized
applications. Teams must still consider data compatibility, licensing,
distribution shift, evaluation quality, and the compute cost of adaptation.

## How it works

Select a pretrained model, adapt its input and output layers as needed,
then train on target examples. Parameters may remain frozen, be updated
partially, or be fine-tuned end-to-end. Validate on data representative of
the target use case.

## Practical example

A vision model pretrained on general images can be adapted to classify
defects in manufactured parts. Compare frozen-feature and fine-tuned
approaches using a held-out test set from the relevant production setting.

## Common misconceptions

- Pretraining on a large dataset does not ensure the model transfers well
  to every target domain.
- Fine-tuning can cause forgetting or overfitting, especially with small
  or mismatched target datasets.
